newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end weak in featureless trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end weak in featureless trade.

text.p: The Singapore stock market ended weak in featureless trade on Tuesday, dealers said.

They said the foreign tranche of national carrier SIA Ltd continued to be battered on heavy volumes due to bearishness over its future earnings prospects. Brokers still advised clients to avoid the stock. SIA Ltd foreign ended S$0.50 down at S$12.50 on 3.7 million shares.

Dealers said newly-listed shares Labroy Marine and Delifrance, were still well-received and actively traded. Labroy ended S$0.01 up at S$1.15 on about five million shares, while Delifrance ended S$0.02 up at S$1.02 on 2.7 million shares.
After trading to a low at 2,054.61, the Straits Times Industrials Index inched up to close flat at 2,061.98. Turnover was a light 79 million shares. Decliners swamped gainers by 226 to 78.
Dealers said the lower than expected interim profit reported by SIA Ltd, a heavy weight among blue-chips, reinforced the slow-down in Singapore's economy, further depressing sentiment.
Singapore Press Foreign led the losers, shedding S$0.90 to S$23.80 on 306,000 shares. Malaysian Assurance led gainers, rising S$0.65 to S$7.40.
